claim: Physical space has three spatial dimensions
justification: Taken as the starting ontology, not derived by this milestone.
A PBUF premise; existence alone fixes neither representation nor component count.

claim: The microscopic state has exactly three real components
justification: Three-dimensional space permits scalar, vector, tensor, and larger microscopic states; dimension matching is not a theorem.

claim: Each component is associated with one spatial direction
justification: Requires q to be a spatial vector/covector and a choice of basis; components are basis-dependent, while q is geometric.

claim: A faithful linear SO(3) vector realization needs at least three real components
justification: SO(3) has no faithful real representation in dimensions 1 or 2; its defining three-dimensional representation is faithful. The premise that q must be faithful and linear is additional.
Even after selecting the vector representation, dynamics, parity, locality, couplings, and field content remain open; non-vector realizations also satisfy the base ontology.

claim: g_dev=1/137 is an intrinsic microscopic coupling
justification: No supplied symmetry, normalization, action, or renormalization prescription derives or operationally isolates it.

claim: g_dev directly normalizes the corrected CORE-001 linear source
justification: The source term is -epsilon_* g_dev eta e.q; no independent coupling multiplier or inverse-rescaling freedom remains.

claim: The current theory identifies 1/137 as a separately measurable parameter
justification: The normalized microscopic equation is sensitive directly to g_dev, but no supplied principle derives its numerical value or links it to an independently completed downstream observable.

claim: u=C_L[e.q] is a scalar continuum deformation
justification: It is rotationally scalar only when q and the matter-selected e transform together and the kernel is isotropic and normalized.

claim: A direction-free nonzero linear map from a spatial vector q to a scalar u exists
justification: No nonzero SO(3)-invariant linear functional on the vector representation exists; one must add e, use derivatives such as div(q), or use a nonlinear invariant such as |q|.

claim: The long-wave scalar equation K u-div(G grad u)=s(rho) follows
justification: Conditional on the projection, stable analytic energy, locality, isotropy, scale separation, and decoupling of other modes; coefficients and source law are not predicted.
